en.title: Two Italians killed in Kuwait drone strike as Iran denies involvement
en.dek: Iranian-made drones targeted Kuwaiti military installations, killing two Italian technicians working for Rheinmetall, while Tehran denies responsibility.
facts: Two Italian Rheinmetall technicians killed in Kuwait drone strike on 26 November 2026
Iranian-made drones targeted Kuwaiti military installations including an air-defence detection station
Iran's foreign ministry assigned responsibility for the attack to Iran
Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi called the Kuwait incident "suspicious" and a "pre-cooked recipe" for war
Italian FM Antonio Ta confirmed the drones were Iranian-made and targeted the air-defence detection station
Iran denied involvement, according to BBC and CNA
body: On 26 November 2026, a drone strike in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working for the German company Rheinmetall, according to Italy's foreign ministry and multiple international outlets.

Italian and international media reported the strike involved Iranian-made drones targeting Kuwaiti military installations, including an air-defence detection station where the technicians were working.

Iran's foreign ministry assigned responsibility for the attack to Iran, while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described the incident as "suspicious" and suggested it looked like a "pre-cooked recipe" for war, according to Al Jazeera.
The New York Times and Los Angeles Times described the strike as an Iranian drone attack, citing officials, while Iran denied involvement, according to BBC and CNA.

Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Ta stated that several Iranian-made drones targeted Kuwaiti military installations, including the air-defence detection station where the two technicians were working at the time of the strike.
Tagesschau reported that Italy has assigned responsibility for the attack to Iran, while Tehran continues to deny involvement.
en.context: A drone strike in Kuwait on 26 November 2026 killed two Italian technicians from the German company Rheinmetall who were working at a military site. Iranian-made drones targeted Kuwaiti military installations, and responsibility for the attack has been assigned to Iran by Italian officials, while Iran denies involvement.
